problem:
Given a list of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two different elements whose sum equals target. Assume exactly one such pair exists; the indices may be returned in any order.

Example: nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9 -> [0, 1]
Example: nums = [3, 2, 4], target = 6 -> [1, 2]

data.title: Two Sum
data.summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer target, return the indices of two different elements that add up to target. Exactly one answer exists.

data.generator_code:
def generate(rng, n):
    n = max(2, n)
    nums = [rng.randint(-20, 20) for _ in range(n)]
    i, j = rng.sample(range(n), 2)
    return [nums, nums[i] + nums[j]]

def generate_worst(rng, n):
    return [list(range(1, n + 1)), 2 * n - 1]
data.checker_code:
def check(args, got, expected):
    nums, target = args
    return (isinstance(got, list) and len(got) == 2 and got[0] != got[1]
            and nums[got[0]] + nums[got[1]] == target)

data.pattern_summary: Store what you've already seen in a dictionary so that 'have I seen X?' takes constant time instead of a scan.

pattern_options.name: Hash map lookup
pattern_options.feedback: Each number needs one specific partner (target - x). A dictionary answers 'have I seen that partner?' instantly.

pattern_options.name: Two pointers on a sorted array
pattern_options.feedback: Works for the sum, but sorting loses the original indices you must return, and costs O(n log n).

pattern_options.name: Sliding window
pattern_options.feedback: Windows are for contiguous ranges; the two numbers can be anywhere.

pattern_options.name: Dynamic programming
pattern_options.feedback: There are no overlapping subproblems to build up; it's a lookup.

signals.hint: Fixing one number fixes its partner exactly: target - x.
You must remember positions, not just values.

data.brute_force_idea: Try every pair (i, j) with i < j and check whether they add up to target.
data.brute_force_why: For each of the n elements, the inner loop scans the rest: n·(n-1)/2 pairs.
data.bottleneck: For every i, the inner loop re-scans the array looking for one specific value, target - nums[i]. The same elements get searched over and over.
bottleneck_hints: Which line runs the most times as the array grows?
For a fixed i, what exact value is the inner loop searching for?
Searching for a known value by scanning is slow. What finds a value instantly?

data.insight: Instead of re-scanning for target - x, remember every value seen so far in a dictionary. Checking for the partner becomes one O(1) lookup, so the inner loop disappears.

derivation.note: Dictionary membership is a hash lookup.
Dictionary insert is a hash write.

data.time_summary: n iterations × O(1) work each = O(n). The step counts double when n doubles (linear), while the brute force quadruples (quadratic).
data.space_summary: The dictionary can hold up to n entries: O(n) extra space.
data.takeaway: When each element needs one specific partner, store what you've seen in a hash map and look the partner up instead of searching for it.
mistakes: Building the whole map first can pair an element with itself (target = 2·x).
Assuming numbers are non-negative and pruning with x > target.
